properties.name: streamguard.enabled
properties.description: Whether StreamGuard is enabled. When false the application is left untouched.

properties.name: streamguard.web.enabled
properties.description: Whether to serve the JSON API and dashboard. Monitoring and alerting run either way.

properties.name: streamguard.web.base-path
properties.description: Path the dashboard is served at. The JSON API lives under '<base-path>/api'. Must start with '/' and not end with '/'.

properties.name: streamguard.routes.include
properties.description: Path patterns to monitor, in Spring MVC syntax such as '/api/**'. Empty monitors every request.

properties.name: streamguard.routes.exclude
properties.description: Path patterns never monitored, even when included.

properties.name: streamguard.routes.auth
properties.description: Login and token routes. Repeated 401/403 responses from one client on these are reported as brute force.

properties.name: streamguard.windows.bucket-size-seconds
properties.description: Resolution of the sliding windows, in seconds.

properties.name: streamguard.windows.max-window-seconds
properties.description: Longest window that can be queried, in seconds.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.evaluation-window-seconds
properties.description: Length of the closed windows compared for anomalies, availability and forecasting.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.min-requests
properties.description: Minimum requests in a window before it is evaluated for anomalies and error-rate alerts.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.error-spike-min-z
properties.description: Standard errors an error-rate rise must clear (one-sided two-proportion z-test) before ERROR_SPIKE fires. 3.09 is a 0.1% chance per window of alerting on noise; 0 disables the check.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.error-rate-floor-pct
properties.description: Lowest previous error rate ERROR_SPIKE compares against, so 0% baselines don't make single errors look like spikes.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.error-rate-threshold-pct
properties.description: Error rate (0-100) that opens an ERROR_RATE_HIGH alert, so a route that keeps failing is reported. Above 100 disables it.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.error-rate-long-window-seconds
properties.description: Window the error-rate threshold must also hold over before ERROR_RATE_HIGH opens, so short bursts don't. At least the evaluation window, at most max-window-seconds.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.error-rate-recovery-pct
properties.description: Error rate a window must be below to count toward resolving ERROR_RATE_HIGH. Must not exceed the threshold.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.error-rate-resolve-windows
properties.description: Consecutive windows below the recovery rate before ERROR_RATE_HIGH resolves.

properties.name: streamguard.detection.error-rate-repeat-interval-seconds
properties.description: How often an open ERROR_RATE_HIGH alert is raised again, in seconds. 0 never repeats.

properties.name: streamguard.forecast.base-alpha
properties.description: Resting EWMA smoothing factor, between 0 and 1. Higher reacts faster.

properties.name: streamguard.forecast.spike-sigma
properties.description: How many deviations above the forecast count as a FORECAST_SPIKE.

properties.name: streamguard.forecast.min-requests
properties.description: Minimum requests in a window before forecast spikes are raised.

properties.name: streamguard.filter.trust-forwarded-for
properties.description: Read the client IP from X-Forwarded-For. Only enable behind a proxy you control.

properties.name: streamguard.alert.webhook-urls
properties.description: URLs every alert is POSTed to as JSON.

properties.name: streamguard.alert.allow-runtime-updates
properties.description: Allow replacing the webhook list through the HTTP API. Off by default, since anyone who can reach the API could redirect alerts.
